what_happened: Web search confirmed four major 2026 TypeScript-toolchain shifts not reliable from training data alone: TypeScript 7.0 (Go-native tsgo) reached GA July 2026 and is now what 'tsc' itself resolves to in typescript@7.x; ESLint v10 (Feb 2026) removed eslintrc support entirely, flat config is now the sole format; Bun's text-based bun.lock became the default lockfile format in Bun 1.2, superseding the legacy binary bun.lockb; Vite 8 (stable March 2026) made Rolldown the default production bundler, replacing esbuild+Rollup. These directly change several toolchain-detection matrix rows and were verified before drafting the matrix rather than assumed from stale pretraining.

Plan-authoring audit of the research report found two verified coverage gaps against the dispatch's own REQUIRED OUTCOMES: (a) Outcome 2's manifest field-to-consumer table omits merge_targets per-entry sub-fields, and section_id appears zero times in the report despite being present in all five surveyed manifests and mandated by task 621's spec; (b) Outcome 6's detection matrix has no signal for Node native TypeScript type-stripping, no row for a project with no tsconfig.json, and no erasable-syntax constraint note -- exactly the profile task 622 is specified to validate against. Both gaps were closed into dedicated plan phases (2 and 3) rather than deferred downstream.

Phase 1 re-derived all five load-bearing mechanical claims and both completeness-discharge sweeps in the research report against live source (manifest.lua REQUIRED_FIELDS/early-returns, skill-base.sh hook contract incl. 5 positional args and literal final return 0, manifest-routing-lib.sh routing_lookup_flat sibling-not-wrapper ladder, merge.lua append_index_entries upsert-by-path). Every claim held exactly; no in-place correction was needed. The manifest sweep for unlisted keys found nothing beyond the already-scoped merge_targets.{entry}.section_id sub-field gap Phase 2 is tasked with closing -- confirmed section_id appears in all five manifests' merge_targets entries and zero times in the report.

Phase 1 task list in the plan names a non-existent path agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/skill-base.sh for the lifecycle-hook re-derivation; the real file is agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/skill-base.sh (no /lib/ segment). Did not block re-derivation since the real file was located by search; noted in the plan's own checklist annotation rather than left silent.

Phase 2 tracing section_id's actual consumer found two load-bearing report claims did not hold: (1) the Outcome 2 table's merge_targets row cites 'loader.lua's process_merge_targets()/reverse_merge_targets()' but these are local functions defined in init.lua, not loader.lua (confirmed: grep for both names across lua/ returns only init.lua definitions and call sites; loader.lua contains neither). (2) section_id was expected (per the plan's own Scope Hypothesis and the dev guide's prose) to be the CLAUDE.md section-delimiting/unload-tracking key, but init.lua's process_merge_targets() explicitly documents skipping section injection for the claudemd merge target entirely -- 'the merge_key entry in merged_sections is intentionally left empty so that reverse_merge_targets has nothing to remove (generation handles removal by regenerating without the unloaded extension's content)' -- and generate_claudemd() (merge.lua) never reads merge_targets.claudemd.section_id at all, only source/target, concatenating full fragment content. The only code that reads section_id (merge.lua's inject_section/remove_section, re-exported by claude/extensions/merge.lua's inject_claudemd_section/remove_claudemd_section) has ZERO callers anywhere in the live load/unload pipeline -- it is dead code from a superseded section-injection design. Both corrections applied in-place to the report in this phase.

Phase 3 verified Node's native TypeScript type-stripping state against the official Node.js docs (nodejs.org/en/learn/typescript/run-natively, cross-checked against a nightly v26 docs build's full version-history table) and the TypeScript 5.8 Microsoft DevBlogs announcement rather than pretraining. Confirmed version thresholds: feature added v22.6.0 (flag-gated via --experimental-strip-types), unflagged default in v23.6.0/v22.18.0, experimental warning removed v24.3.0/v22.18.0, Stable in v24.12.0/v25.2.0. Confirmed the non-erasable construct set (enum, namespace/module with runtime code, parameter properties, decorators as TC39 Stage 3, tsconfig paths aliases) and that Node ignores tsconfig.json entirely for this decision. Confirmed erasableSyntaxOnly is a real TypeScript 5.8 compiler option enforcing the same constraint at tsc time. All added to the detection matrix with sourced citations.

Phase 4's mandated end-to-end consistency read surfaced a third instance of the same loader.lua/init.lua conflation already corrected once in Phase 2: the Outcome 2 table's dependencies row attributed manager.load()'s recursive dependency resolution to loader.lua, but manager.load() is a local function defined inside M.create(config) in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/init.lua (confirmed: grep for 'local manager = {}' and 'function manager.load' both land in init.lua; loader.lua declares no manager table). Corrected in-place. The provides.* row's attribution to loader.lua's M.copy_category was independently re-verified and found correct (M.copy_category is genuinely defined in loader.lua at line 432), so this is not a blanket pattern -- each remaining loader.lua attribution in the table was spot-checked individually.
